title: What Biden Miscalculated About His Classified Documents

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每晚也要带着300件最珍贵的收藏去工作，你会把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个鲜活的、临时搭建的博物馆，里面陈列着精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《今日报》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日。

sentences.en: For the fifth time, classified documents belonging to President Biden have been found outside of a secure government location, this time by FBI agents searching his home.
sentences.zh: 这是第五次发现属于拜登总统的机密文件出现在政府安全地点之外，这一次是由联邦调查局（FBI）特工在他家中搜查时发现的。

sentences.en: My colleague, Mike Scheer, has been trying to understand how Biden chose to handle those discoveries since they began and why, for so long, he left the public in the dark.
sentences.zh: 我的同事迈克·希尔一直在试图了解拜登自这些发现开始以来是如何处理的，以及为什么他让公众在黑暗中蒙蔽了这么久。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, January 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月24日，星期二。

sentences.en: Mike, I want to start with what happened over this past weekend in Wilmington, Delaware.
sentences.zh: 迈克，我想从上周末在特拉华州威尔明顿发生的事情谈起。

sentences.en: Tell us about that.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲那件事。

sentences.en: Yes, it was really quite remarkable, actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，那确实非常引人注目。

sentences.en: The unprecedented FBI search of a sitting president's home for classified documents escalating the legal and political situation for President Biden.
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局对一位在任总统的住所进行史无前例的机密文件搜查，使拜登总统面临的法律和政治局势升级了。

sentences.en: You had the scene of the FBI and a bunch of agents at the invitation of President Biden's personal lawyers.
sentences.zh: 当时的情景是，应拜登总统私人律师的邀请，一群联邦调查局特工出现在现场。

sentences.en: We found out about this on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 我们是在周六得知这一消息的。

sentences.en: FBI agents spent nearly 13 hours scouring his Delaware home on front.
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局特工花了近13个小时搜查他在特拉华州的住所。

sentences.en: Conducting what ended up being a 13-hour search of his personal home in Wilmington, Delaware.
sentences.zh: 最终对他在特拉华州威尔明顿的私人住所进行了长达13小时的搜查。

sentences.en: Investigators reviewed personally handwritten notes, files, papers, binders, memorabilia, to-do lists, schedules, and reminders going back decades.
sentences.zh: 调查人员审查了数十年来他亲手写的笔记、文件、纸张、活页夹、纪念品、待办事项清单、日程安排和提醒事项。

sentences.en: Literally combing through every nook and cranny in every room and office and garage and closet, looking for any indication of additional classified documents
sentences.zh: 他们几乎翻遍了每一个房间、办公室、车库和壁橱的每一个角落，寻找任何可能存在额外机密文件的迹象，

sentences.en: that might have been there improperly.
sentences.zh: 这些文件可能被不当存放于此。

sentences.en: And in fact, they did find them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们确实找到了。

sentences.en: Six items, they said, that included some classification markings.
sentences.zh: 他们说，有六件物品包含了一些机密标记。

sentences.en: Some go back as far as his time in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 有些可以追溯到他在参议院任职期间。

sentences.en: This drip, drip, drip just continues.
sentences.zh: 这种“滴水穿石”式的爆料还在继续。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And for those keeping count, this is now the fifth time in about, let's say, three months that classified documents have been found in President Biden's possession
sentences.zh: 对于那些在统计的人来说，这已经是大约三个月内第五次发现拜登总统持有机密文件了，

sentences.en: in places where they just shouldn't be.
sentences.zh: 而且是在它们本不该出现的地方。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because where they should be are insecure government.
sentences.zh: 因为它们本该在不安全的政府地点，

sentences.en: Locations like the White House.
sentences.zh: 比如白宫。

sentences.en: So at this point, we've clearly reached a moment where the story of Biden and how he has handled classified documents has become something of a rolling public relations
sentences.zh: 所以目前看来，我们显然已经到了这样一个时刻：拜登处理机密文件的方式已经演变成了一场持续不断的公关

sentences.en: and legal mess for this president.
sentences.zh: 和法律灾难，让这位总统深陷其中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And the amazing thing is what has ended up transpiring is exactly what they had hoped to head off when they discussed how to handle the discovery of these documents
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，最终发生的事情正是他们在讨论如何处理这些文件发现时，

sentences.en: at the very beginning of this situation.
sentences.zh: 在这一情况最开始时就希望避免的。

sentences.en: Well, Mike, I want you to explain that because I know that you and a few of our colleagues have spent the past couple of days trying to both piece that together and understand it.
sentences.zh: 迈克，我想请你解释一下，因为我知道你和我们的几位同事过去几天一直在试图拼凑并理解这一点。

sentences.en: the calculations made by President Biden and those around him about the best way to approach a very bad situation, which is, you know, classified documents
sentences.zh: 拜登总统及其身边人对于处理这种糟糕局面的最佳方式所做的考量，也就是，你知道，机密文件

sentences.en: found where they shouldn't be in his orbit.
sentences.zh: 出现在了他不该出现的地方。

sentences.en: So tell us about that.
sentences.zh: 所以给我们讲讲吧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So there's been a lot of reporting about this over the last couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 过去几周关于这件事的报道非常多。

sentences.en: What we had decided was that we would look at a very specific period of time as this has all developed.
sentences.zh: 我们决定关注这一事件发展过程中一个非常特定的时间段。

sentences.en: And that is what we found to be the 68 days between when the first set of documents were discovered in early November of last year
sentences.zh: 那就是我们发现的这68天，从去年11月初首次发现第一批文件，

sentences.en: and when the White House finally told the public about it in early January.
sentences.zh: 到今年1月初白宫最终向公众披露此事之间的时间。

sentences.en: And in essence, what we found was that the president and a very, very small circle of legal and political advisors had decided that they could settle the matter
sentences.zh: 本质上，我们发现总统和极少数法律及政治顾问决定，如果他们能在每一步都与司法部充分合作，回答调查人员可能想问的每一个问题，尽他们所能，

sentences.en: quickly and quietly if they were super cooperative with the Department of Justice at every turn, answer every question the investigators might want, really everything they could do
sentences.zh: 他们就能迅速而安静地解决这个问题，

sentences.en: to stand in contrast to the way former President Trump had handled a similar investigation into classified documents found at his home in Mar-a-Lago.
sentences.zh: 从而与前总统特朗普处理其海湖庄园家中发现机密文件的调查方式形成鲜明对比。

sentences.en: The former president and his lawyers initially resisted efforts by the Justice Department to look into it.
sentences.zh: 前总统及其律师最初抵制了司法部的调查努力。

sentences.en: They refused to allow searches of the House, which then led to a raid of his property and subpoenas.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝允许搜查住所，这随后导致了对其财产的突击搜查和传票。

sentences.en: And so what the Biden administration thought was if they did the opposite, they cooperate fully with the department, hopefully would avoid a big, sprawling public investigation.
sentences.zh: 因此，拜登政府认为，如果他们采取相反的做法，与司法部充分合作，就有望避免一场大规模的公开调查。

sentences.en: Ultimately, they would not have to disclose anything to the public because ultimately they hoped it would just go away.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们不必向公众披露任何信息，因为他们希望这件事能就此平息。

sentences.en: And of course, that's not what happened.
sentences.zh: 当然，事情并没有如他们所愿。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: So the thinking here from within the Biden world is that with this Trump classified document investigation playing out in a parallel universe, they would do everything differently
sentences.zh: 所以拜登团队内部的想法是，随着特朗普机密文件调查在平行宇宙中展开，他们会在法律意义上采取完全不同的做法，

sentences.en: in a legal sense and thus not have to tell the public pretty much anything.
sentences.zh: 从而不必向公众透露任何实质内容。

sentences.en: And it would all just work out.
sentences.zh: 一切都会迎刃而解。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it turned out that they committed a series of miscalculations.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，他们犯了一系列误判。

sentences.en: They miscalculated how many documents would ultimately be found.
sentences.zh: 他们误判了最终会发现多少文件。

sentences.en: They miscalculated the way the Department of Justice would respond.
sentences.zh: 他们误判了司法部的反应方式。

sentences.en: And ultimately, they miscalculated the way in which people would see
sentences.zh: 最终，他们误判了人们看待

sentences.en: President Biden's handling of documents versus President Trump's.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统处理文件的方式与特朗普总统处理方式时的态度。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, Mike, let's talk through what this strategy has looked like in practice from day one and how we arrive at those miscalculations that you just summarized.
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，让我们谈谈这种策略从第一天起在实践中是什么样子的，以及我们是如何得出你刚才总结的那些误判的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So it all starts on November 2nd.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于11月2日。

sentences.en: That's six days before the midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 那是中期选举前六天。

sentences.en: Very important for President Biden.
sentences.zh: 这对拜登总统非常重要。

sentences.en: That's when members of the president's team are cleaning out an office in Washington at this think tank that he had worked at before becoming president
sentences.zh: 当时总统团队的成员正在清理华盛顿一家智库的办公室，他在担任总统前曾在这里工作，

sentences.en: and had essentially been untouched for a couple of years now.
sentences.zh: 这个办公室基本上已经有几年没人动过了。

sentences.en: They're cleaning that out.
sentences.zh: 他们正在清理那里。

sentences.en: They find a handful of classified documents.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了几份机密文件。

sentences.en: They did immediately send the documents to the National Archives, which keeps these kinds of government papers.
sentences.zh: 他们立即将这些文件送交了国家档案馆，该机构负责保管这类政府文件。

sentences.en: The National Archives informed the Department of Justice.
sentences.zh: 国家档案馆通知了司法部。

sentences.en: But it wasn't until about November 9th or 10th that the Justice Department then gets back in touch with the president's lawyers, says, hey, we are now looking into this.
sentences.zh: 但直到11月9日或10日左右，司法部才与总统的律师取得联系，说，嘿，我们现在正在调查这件事。

sentences.en: And that is when the president and this very small group of aides had to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，总统和这群极少数的助手必须做出决定。

sentences.en: What are we going to do?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: And the decision was, we're going to completely cooperate, but we're going to be quiet.
sentences.zh: 决定是：我们将完全配合，但我们要保持安静。

sentences.en: We are not going to make anything about this public.
sentences.zh: 我们不会向公众透露任何关于这件事的信息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is probably
sentences.zh: 这可能是

sentences.en: the biggest of these early moments, because when the Department of Justice tells the president that it's looking into something, essentially that it's investigating
sentences.zh: 早期最关键的时刻之一，因为当司法部告诉总统它正在调查某事，本质上是在调查

sentences.en: the president's conduct, that is, in theory, a very natural moment to tell the public.
sentences.zh: 总统的行为时，理论上这是一个告诉公众的非常自然的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah, a natural moment to tell the public and something pretty significant, especially in the light of the investigation that was going on to his predecessor, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个告诉公众的自然时刻，也是一件相当重大的事情，特别是在针对他前任的调查背景下，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's hard to imagine that at that moment, they didn't at least have a sense of the importance that this could be.
sentences.zh: 所以很难想象在那个时刻，他们至少没有意识到这可能的重要性。

sentences.en: So how have you come to understand the logic of Biden and his tight circle of advisors deciding not to tell the public?
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何理解拜登及其核心顾问圈决定不告诉公众的逻辑的呢？

sentences.en: That the Department of Justice is now investigating its handling of these classified documents.
sentences.zh: 即司法部现在正在调查其对这些机密文件的处理。

sentences.en: So their explanation now of those early decisions was that they essentially were trying to follow scrupulously all of the rules that the Justice Department
sentences.zh: 他们现在对那些早期决定的解释是，他们基本上是在试图严格遵守司法部

sentences.en: usually has about ongoing investigations, which is to say not to talk about them.
sentences.zh: 通常对正在进行的调查所持有的所有规则，也就是说，不要谈论它们。

sentences.en: But there was also a second reason, because they thought that if they went public and tried to explain what had happened in the president's actions, folks at the Justice Department
sentences.zh: 但还有第二个原因，因为他们认为如果他们公开并试图解释总统的行为，司法部的人

sentences.en: would see that as potentially being an attempt to unduly influence the course of this investigation, because, of course, the president is the attorney general's boss.
sentences.zh: 会认为这可能是在试图不当影响调查进程，因为毕竟总统是司法部长的上司。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And anything that he says publicly could be seen as an attempt to put his thumb on the scales of justice.
sentences.zh: 他公开说的任何话都可能被视为试图在正义的天平上施加影响。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So they're saying our hands are tied.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说我们的手被束缚住了。

sentences.en: And from what you're saying, that makes a certain amount of sense, at least in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 从你的话来看，这在某种程度上是有道理的，至少在开始时是这样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it does, to a degree.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种程度上确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, there is no question that Department of Justice prefers to do these kinds of investigations quietly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毫无疑问，司法部更喜欢悄悄地进行这类调查。

sentences.en: It makes it easier to find the right people to talk to.
sentences.zh: 这使得找到合适的人交谈更容易。

sentences.en: They don't have to compete with the swirl of news every day.
sentences.zh: 他们不必每天与新闻漩涡竞争。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, the White House had to make that decision themselves.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，白宫必须自己做出那个决定。

sentences.en: Are they going to inform the public?
sentences.zh: 他们要通知公众吗？

sentences.en: Because it's ultimately a public relations call to make, and that was the one they made, to stay silent.
sentences.zh: 因为这最终是一个公关决定，而这就是他们做出的决定：保持沉默。

sentences.en: Right, because you're saying there's nothing that prevents the White House from coming out, from someone standing at a podium in the White House briefing room and saying,
sentences.zh: 没错，因为你是说没有什么能阻止白宫站出来，没有什么能阻止某人站在白宫简报室的讲台上说，

sentences.en: we have something to announce.
sentences.zh: 我们有事情要宣布。

sentences.en: We've found documents.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了文件。

sentences.en: The Department of Justice is looking at them.
sentences.zh: 司法部正在查看它们。

sentences.en: We don't have a whole lot more to say.
sentences.zh: 我们没有太多要说的。

sentences.en: Sorry, it might pollute an investigation.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，这可能会污染调查。

sentences.en: But we owe you this information.
sentences.zh: 但我们有义务告知你们这些信息。

sentences.en: So you're welcome.
sentences.zh: 所以不客气。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They could have done that in November, and they chose not to.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以在11月那样做，但他们选择了不这样做。

sentences.en: Okay, so once they choose this strategy of cooperate, but stay silent, what's the next big moment?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么一旦他们选择了这种“配合但保持沉默”的策略，下一个重大时刻是什么？

sentences.en: So the next moment comes just before Christmas, on December 20th.
sentences.zh: 下一个时刻出现在圣诞节前夕，12月20日。

sentences.en: The president's lawyers having hoped that the Justice Department would say, hey, we finished our inquiry.
sentences.zh: 总统的律师曾希望司法部会说，嘿，我们完成了调查。

sentences.en: This is nothing.
sentences.zh: 这没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: We're going to go away.
sentences.zh: 我们要结案了。

sentences.en: And that hasn't happened.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有发生。

sentences.en: The Justice Department is still looking into the case.
sentences.zh: 司法部仍在调查此案。

sentences.en: And the president's lawyers decide, you know what, it's probably time to search other places that documents might be, including the president's homes, one in Wilmington, Delaware,
sentences.zh: 总统的律师决定，你知道吗，现在可能是时候搜查其他可能存放文件的地方了，包括总统的住所，一个在特拉华州威尔明顿，

sentences.en: and one in Rehoboth Beach, Delaware.
sentences.zh: 另一个在特拉华州里霍博斯海滩。

sentences.en: And so the president's lawyers go ahead, they search both places, and they do find some documents in Wilmington at the president's home.
sentences.zh: 于是总统的律师继续进行了搜查，他们确实在威尔明顿总统家中发现了一些文件。

sentences.en: But the president and those same aides decide, we're going to continue with our strategy.
sentences.zh: 但总统和那些同样的助手决定，我们要继续我们的策略。

sentences.en: Cooperation and silence.
sentences.zh: 合作与沉默。

sentences.en: We're not going to tell the public.
sentences.zh: 我们不会告诉公众。

sentences.en: In other words, they do tell the Justice Department, hey, we found a lot more documents in this house in Wilmington, Delaware, but they do not tell us that fact.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们确实告诉了司法部，嘿，我们在特拉华州威尔明顿的这所房子里发现了更多文件，但他们没有告诉我们这个事实。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And you have a situation now where whether they sort of realized it in full or not, they were clearly playing with fire at this point because, you know, the Justice Department
sentences.zh: 现在的情况是，无论他们是否完全意识到这一点，他们显然在此时是在玩火，因为，你知道，司法部

sentences.en: clearly wasn't going away.
sentences.zh: 显然不会就此罢休。

sentences.en: It was continuing to examine and look into this.
sentences.zh: 它在继续审查和调查此事。

sentences.en: And so the decision that they made originally in November and now we're sticking to in December was becoming riskier and riskier.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最初在11月做出的决定，以及现在在12月坚持的决定，正变得越来越危险。

sentences.en: Mike, at this point, because you are trying to reconstruct this period,
sentences.zh: 迈克，在这一点上，因为你正在试图重构这段时期，

sentences.en: does anyone inside the White House go to this small group of advisors and say, you know, it's probably time to tell the public what's going on?
sentences.zh: 白宫内部有没有人去问这群核心顾问，说，你知道，现在可能是时候告诉公众发生了什么了？
